text: Make sure the VIN can be read back no matter which session the module is in, and that asking for the VIN, the part number and the serial number in a single request returns all three values.
The central-locking auto-relock setting may only be changed from the extended mode, after the unlock step has been completed; anything other than on or off must be refused.
The wiper sensitivity calibration value accepts settings from 1 up to 5 and nothing else, so 0 and 6 have to bounce, and the write needs the extended-mode unlock first.
Once the lighting self-test has been kicked off the tester can poll its outcome or abort it; asking for the outcome or stopping it before it was ever started must be rejected.

Restoring the module's non-volatile memory to factory state takes a while: the module first says it is busy and later delivers the final answer. It is only available in the flash session after the programming-level unlock.
After three wrong keys in the seed-key handshake the module must stop accepting attempts for ten seconds, even if the correct key is then sent, and accept it again after the wait.

The test engineer must be able to list the trouble codes in fault memory by status mask, then wipe fault memory and confirm nothing is reported afterwards; other ways of querying the fault memory are not offered.
If nothing is sent for about five seconds while in a non-default mode the module falls back to the default session; periodic keep-alive messages must prevent that.
After the session has timed out back to default, the earlier unlock must be gone, so a write to the interior light brightness is refused until the handshake is redone.
After power-cycling the module with either kind of reset, it comes back in the default session with the unlock lost, and the active-session value reads default.
notes: state after hard and soft reset

text: A keep-alive (0x3E) sent with the suppress-reply bit set must produce no response at all but must still restart the session timer.
The door actuator calibration (0x0202) may only run in extended mode, after unlocking, and only while the car is parked; with the car moving it must be refused.
The variant coding value can be changed only in the flash session after the programming-level unlock; the full 16-bit range is acceptable and the new value must read back.
The door lock status should be readable by the tester but not changeable by anyone unauthorised.
notes: Ambiguous: which door (driver, passenger or both) and what unauthorised means. Labels assume both lock-state DIDs, read OK, write refused (not writable at all).

text: Wiping the fault memory should be refused when it is not allowed.
notes: Ambiguous: not allowed when. Labels assume the case where the clear service is not offered in the flash session.

text: The module should store a freeze-frame snapshot with every trouble code and report it on request.
notes: Unsupported by spec (no freeze-frame/snapshot defined); empty targets on purpose.
